question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=3,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(3) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,3,4⟩, \\ N(3) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,4,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(3) & =T(3)\times N(3) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,3,4⟩\times \frac{1}{5}⟨0,4,-3⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{25}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}⟨(-9-16),-(0-0),(0-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{25}⟨-25,0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
